title: Create a fixed resource window and verify its readback
summary: Create small fictional schedules and verify their actual stored values and coverage counts.
prerequisites: Use a fictional practice department and existing shift create/view/update permissions.
Use existing groups, roles and members; prepare future dates and identifiable practice entries.

scenes.title: Open the fixed resource window
scenes.narration: Use Add Static Shift from the shared Shifts calendar when you need a fixed resource window. This is separate from the recurring group schedule used for people and role minimums. Our practice entry will cover November fourth to fifth and use a separate training unit. Start with a clear purpose and an explicit start and end. Keep the entry easy to identify so another administrator can review the resource, date and context before relying on it.
scenes.practice: Find Add Static Shift and define a fictional resource window before opening the form.

scenes.title: Prepare a separate practice resource
scenes.narration: Prepare an identifiable practice unit through New Unit. Here its name says Training Only, Static demo unit, followed by the exercise date. Choose the existing Engine type, leave Station at No Station and keep Roles empty. Save the new entry once, then find and reopen it to verify those choices. The returned unit has the default Available status. This separate software resource lets us demonstrate scheduling without changing another apparatus or its crew. No device position or hardware tracking setup is part of this example.

scenes.title: Use a readable name and calendar color
scenes.narration: On New Static Shift, enter Training Only, Static November fourth as the name. The short name stays readable in this form. Choose a light yellow background color. The help reminds you that calendar text is black, so review contrast along with the color itself. A distinctive name and color make the entry easier to recognize when it appears alongside personnel shifts. They are labels for the schedule; they do not change the unit’s operational status.

scenes.title: Give the resource window explicit context
required_labels: TRAINING ONLY. Fictional scheduling and equipment-window software exercise. No deployment, travel, work, expense, payment or live apparatus-availability claim.
scenes.narration: Description is a separate rich-text editor. Explain why the resource window exists and what another reader should verify. This example identifies a fictional scheduling exercise and makes clear that it does not record deployment, travel, work, expense or payment. Keep that context attached to the schedule itself. A useful description tells the next administrator what the entry represents without requiring them to infer its purpose from a color or short name. Review the complete text before creating the entry.

scenes.title: Verify both dates and the selected resource
scenes.narration: Set Start Date and Time to November fourth, twenty twenty-six, at nine in the morning, and End Date and Time to November fifth at nine. Check the displayed values after leaving each field; this picker displays a year, month, day and twenty-four-hour time. Under Units, select only the new training unit and verify its visible chip. Read both endpoints and the resource name together before using Create Static Shift. The form’s travel and availability help describes its intended scheduling meaning; verify operational effects separately.

scenes.title: Inspect the newly saved day
scenes.narration: Choose Create Static Shift once. In the shared calendar, open the new entry. View Static Shift Day shows the name, description, November fourth at nine, and the selected training unit. The Unit Role table is empty because this unit has no configured roles or filled positions in the exercise. Read the saved identity and association before making another change. This view demonstrates the created scheduling entry; it does not demonstrate a real deployment or an automatic change to another unit’s availability.

scenes.title: Stop when the reopened editor disagrees
scenes.narration: Reopen Edit Static Shift and compare its values before submitting an update. In this example, the editor shows three in the morning instead of the nine shown on the saved day, and its Units selection is blank. Stop here. Do not submit an editor whose values disagree with the entry you intended to maintain. The visible warning also says that editing clears existing assignments or signups and reapplies the settings. Resolve the discrepancy and review the intended result before attempting an update.

scenes.title: Adapt the fixed-window review to your work
scenes.narration: Chicago Fire can use a reviewed resource window for a software equipment exercise. Community care and mental health teams can coordinate operational vehicle support without patient information. Search and rescue can schedule support equipment; security teams can identify equipment windows; wildland crews can plan support resources; and industrial response teams can coordinate facility drill equipment. Keep the resource identity, dates and purpose clear. Confirm the saved result and resolve conflicting readbacks before further edits. The surrounding operational decisions still need their own appropriate review.
